New Physics-Based Co-op Title Announced

Developer The Kingsdom has officially announced Ratata, an upcoming four-player cooperative game that combines physics-driven chaos with an '80s crime heist aesthetic. Players step into the paws of an animal gang working to pay off a debt to a mafia toad. The game is currently in development for PC and can be played either as a solo experience or with up to four players.

Gameplay revolves around planning and executing heists under unpredictable physical conditions. Players must choose from a roster of anthropomorphic animals, build up their garage base, acquire targeted items, pack a getaway truck, and successfully deliver the goods. According to the developers, the title embraces a cartoony art style designed to match its chaotic mechanical framework.

Character Mechanics and Hazards

Each playable animal in Ratata features distinct attributes, including varying sizes, strengths, speeds, special abilities, and even differing driver's license statuses. The developers note that character selection plays a direct role in mission success, as certain animals are better suited for specific tasks while proving disastrous for others.

During missions, players will encounter a variety of obstacles and environmental hazards. Confirmed challenges include sneaking past security guards, dodging traps, and evading aggressive adversaries such as fast-moving squirrels described as "crazy granny squirrels."

What Is Known and What Remains Unconfirmed

While the announcement provides a clear look at the premise and artistic direction, several details about the title remain unavailable:

  • Confirmed: Ratata is developed by The Kingsdom for PC, supports solo and up to four-player online or local co-op, features physics-based mechanics, and has an official Steam page available for wishlisting.
  • Unknown: A specific release date, pricing structure, system requirements, and confirmation of additional platform releases beyond PC have not yet been announced.

Practical Implications and How to Verify

For players interested in tracking the game's progress, the primary official avenue is the Steam marketplace, where the title can be added to personal wishlists to receive future updates from the developers. Because the game is still early in its public lifecycle, readers should rely directly on official developer announcements rather than unverified speculation regarding launch windows or platform expansions.

To read the original announcement and view the initial trailer and screenshots, visit the [IGN Report](https://www.ign.com/articles/ratata-a-4-player-physics-chaos-co-op-game-where-you-play-as-anthropomorphic-animals-announced).
